@@ -1,75 +0,0 @@
-= 00003 Runtime Renderer Minutes and Specification
-
-Date: 2026-03-05
-
-Team: University Professor, Software Engineer, Technical Writer
-
-Goal: remove runtime `Code.eval_quoted/3` from Stem evaluation APIs and execute templates through compiled renderer functions for better speed and security posture.
-
-include::common/includes/_doc-policy.adoc[]
-
-== Meeting Minutes
-
-. Problem statement confirmed: `Stem.eval_string/3` and `Stem.eval_file/3` depended on `Code.eval_quoted/3` for every call.
-. Decision: keep `compile_string/2` API unchanged, but switch evaluation to cached runtime modules with `render/1`.
-. Constraint: preserve existing behavior for assigns, helpers, loops (`this`, `@index`), and file/line metadata as much as possible.
-. Additional guard agreed: reject unsupported parent traversal syntax (`../`) at compile time.
-
-== Specification Draft
-
-=== Functional Scope
-
-- `eval_string/3` and `eval_file/3` must execute without calling `Code.eval_quoted/3`.
-- Runtime renderer modules are cached by template compile context.
-- Existing compile-time macros (`function_from_string/5`, `function_from_file/5`) remain unchanged.
-- Runtime binding visibility must support:
-* direct binding variables (example: `bar`),
-* assigns access (example: `{{bar}}` / smart-engine resolution),
-* helper context variables (`this`, `@index`) in loops.
-- Expressions containing `../` in Stem expression tokens must raise `CompileError`.
-
-=== Non-Goals
-
-- No backward-compatibility layer for unsupported parent traversal semantics.
-- No redesign of the tokenizer/compiler architecture.
-
-== Implementation Summary
-
-- Replaced runtime eval path in `Stem.do_eval/3` with cached `render/1` module dispatch.
-- Added runtime module cache via `:persistent_term`.
-- Added AST rewrite for `binding()` calls:
-* now merges runtime bindings with lexical binding context so both explicit bindings and loop locals are visible.
-- Added AST rewrite for `__ENV__.file` to preserve caller-provided file option semantics.
-- Added compile-time guard for unsupported `../` traversal tokens.
-- Added regression test: handlebars variable resolution from direct runtime binding.
-
-== Validation
-
-- Test suite used:
-* `test/stem_test.exs`
-* `test/stem/template_examples_test.exs`
-* `test/stem/builtin_helpers_guide_test.exs`
-* `test/stem/smart_engine_test.exs`
-* `test/stem_migration_test.exs`
-- Result: all selected tests pass (except existing environment warnings unrelated to this feature).
-
-== Checklist
-
-- [x] Runtime execution no longer uses `Code.eval_quoted/3` in hot path.
-- [x] Binding/assign/helper behavior validated in existing tests.
-- [x] Unsupported `../` path traversal now fails at compile time.
-- [x] Regression test added for `{{bar}}` with direct bindings.
-- [x] README updated with runtime renderer note.
-- [x] Minutes + specification documented.
-
-== Mid-Term Improvements
-
-- Replace broad external-variable prebinding with a more precise free-variable analysis to reduce compiler warnings.
-- Add optional bounded cache policy (size/eviction) for runtime renderer modules.
-- Add benchmark suite comparing old eval flow vs cached renderer path (`eval_string/3`, `eval_file/3`, helpers, loops).
-
-== Next Steps
-
-1. Add micro-benchmarks and publish baseline numbers in `papers/`.
-2. Add security notes describing evaluation model and trust boundaries for template source.
-3. Consider exposing a public API for prebuilding runtime renderer modules for operational warm-up.

@@ -1,47 +0,0 @@
-= 00004 Native Compiler Minutes and Specification
-
-Date: 2026-05-21
-
-Team: University Professor, Software Engineer, Technical Writer
-
-Goal: replace the EEx-backed compilation path with a native `{{ }}` compiler so Stem owns its tokenizer, parser, AST, and code generation.
-
-== Meeting Minutes
-
-. Problem statement confirmed: templates were rewritten into EEx text and run through the EEx tokenizer and compiler, which leaked EEx semantics, escaping markers, and error messages.
-. Decision: build a native pipeline `tokenizer -> parser -> AST -> compiler` that emits Elixir AST directly.
-. Decision: drop the EEx surface entirely, including the `<%= %>` tag family, the `Stem.Engine`/`Stem.SmartEngine` behaviour and custom engines, the EEx tokenizer (`Stem.tokenize/2`), and the `:engine`, `:trim`, and `:parser_options` options.
-. Constraint: preserve the `{{ }}` language already exercised by the test suite (expressions, raw output, comments, raw quotation, `#if`/`#unless`/`#each`/`#with`, `else`, partials, helpers, `this`/`@index`/`@key`, and `../` parent access).
-. Constraint: keep the compile-time-only security model; runtime evaluation stays disabled.
-
-== Specification
-
-=== Pipeline
-
-- `Stem.Tokenizer` scans source into structural tokens with line and column metadata.
-- `Stem.Parser` matches block open/else/close tokens into a `Stem.AST`, expands partials inline with a recursion guard, and reports structural errors.
-- `Stem.Compiler` lowers the AST into quoted Elixir; `Stem.Expression` translates the contents of each tag, and `Stem.Runtime` resolves assigns at runtime.
-
-=== Non-Goals
-
-- No backward-compatibility layer for the removed EEx syntax.
-- No Handlebars-style standalone whitespace control yet; the `:trim` option was removed with the EEx tokenizer.
-
-== Implementation Summary
-
-- Added `Stem.Tokenizer`, `Stem.Parser`, `Stem.AST`, `Stem.Compiler`, `Stem.Expression`, and `Stem.Runtime`.
-- Removed the EEx compiler, engine, smart engine, and the string preprocessor.
-- Rewrote the public surface and module documentation in `lib/stem.ex`.
-- Added a symmetric `helpers` no-op in the function macros and marked loop bindings as generated to keep compilation warning-free.
-- Repaired the standalone-checkout coverage guard so `mix test --cover` runs.
-
-== Validation
-
-- Full suite green via `mix test` (including doctests).
-- Line coverage is 99% via `mix test --cover`, above the 98% threshold.
-
-== Next Steps
-
-. Add Handlebars-style standalone whitespace control.
-. Consider exposing the tokenizer or AST publicly for linting and static analysis.
-. Add micro-benchmarks comparing the native compiler against the previous EEx path.
